summary: TL;DR Good developers’ caution about agentic development comes from knowing that built isn’t the same as working in production. I’ve been surprised by how many excellent developers have been hesitant to go all in on coding agents.
takeaways: Most of the work at the keyboard was directing agents to put this learning into the harness, so the building and testing agents got it right on the next run and they could have more confidence in what they built.
These are people who usually try new ways of working before anyone else and in many cases invent new tools and practices that support building the application well.
In September, a discussion we had on agentic development, which pushed it to its limits, finally helped me see clearly what that fear is.
